findings: fsst.cpp DecompressStrings: the buffer bound is 8 bytes per compressed byte for every string in the batch, plus 32 bytes of slack. That covers the 8-byte unaligned symbol stores, because the buffer space already used is never more than the worst case of the strings already decoded. A single string larger than the 64KB batch cap gets its own batch. Inlined strings are copied into their string_t before their space is reused. `used` is always either 0 or more than 12, so FinalizeShrinkableBuffer releases the right number of bytes. No other arena allocation happens in between, so the head-position assertion holds.

fsst.cpp DecodeString: an escape as the last byte throws instead of reading past the input. The decoder import sets len[] to 1..8 for every code, and code 255 (the escape) never indexes symbol[]. This matches the semantics of the existing fsst_decompress loop. The all-values-inlined case keeps the old path.

column_segment.cpp TrySubstringPrefilter: the needle is the longest literal between '%' and '_' wildcards. Plain ~~ and !~~ have no escape character (LikeOperatorFunction uses its default), so any string the pattern matches must contain that literal. Collated columns are excluded because the first argument must be a bare BOUND_REF. Rows that contain the needle are re-checked with the original expression, so a candidate set that is too large stays correct. In the negated case, NULL rows are rejected and non-NULL rows without the needle pass, which matches NOT LIKE semantics. Runs only cover non-inlined strings, which are never empty. Matches that cross a row boundary are rejected. The SSE loads stay inside hay+hay_len, including the overlapping final block. It falls back to the old path when scan_count > STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE or the vector is not flat.
Both optimisations apply generally to FSST scans and to scan-pushed substring filters. Neither depends on particular queries or data. No timing, settings or tests are touched.
